plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests a 20-layer HfO2/SiO2 dichroic stack optimized for UV reflection (200-400 nm) and SWIR transmission (800-1500 nm). The design principle is recalled from thin-film optics knowledge: alternating high-low index quarter-wave pairs centered on the reflection band, with thickness tuning to broaden the stopband while maintaining transmission outside it. This route continues refinement from prior control iterations, narrowing perturbation bounds to converge on the local optimum near the 0.8279 target score candidate.

routes.title: 20-layer HfO2/SiO2 dichroic refinement with narrowed perturbation bounds
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A 20-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack with individually tunable thicknesses can achieve simultaneous high UV reflection and high SWIR transmission, and further refinement with reduced perturbation bounds (±0.5 nm) will improve target score convergence without destabilizing the solution.
routes.design_principle: Recalled thin-film optics principle: alternating high-low refractive index layers form a Bragg reflector centered at the design wavelength. Quarter-wave optical thickness (n·d = λ₀/4) maximizes reflectance at the center wavelength. For dual-band operation, the reflection band is positioned at UV (center ~300 nm) while SWIR (800-1500 nm) falls outside the stopband for high transmission.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate (20 layers total, alternating starting with HfO2)
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 20 layers, initialized from prior best candidate and tuned within ±0.5 nm perturbation bounds
soft_objectives: Maximize target score combining UV reflection (200-400 nm) and SWIR transmission (800-1500 nm)
Maintain physical validity (positive thicknesses, manufacturable ranges)
Improve best_target_score over prior iteration 0.8279 baseline
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 20 (within 30-layer limit)
Thicknesses expected in 25-55 nm range based on UV quarter-wave design
HfO2 and SiO2 are standard evaporatable/sputterable dielectric materials
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave stack reflectance increases with number of layer pairs
Recalled knowledge: HfO2 refractive index ~2.0-2.1, SiO2 ~1.45-1.5 in visible/NIR
Recalled knowledge: Reflection band center wavelength λ₀ determines layer thickness d = λ₀/(4n)
Recalled knowledge: Wider reflection bandwidth requires more layer pairs or higher index contrast
Recalled knowledge: Transmission outside the stopband is naturally high for lossless dielectric stacks
expected_advantages: Narrower perturbation bounds (±0.5 nm vs prior ±0.8 nm) reduce oscillatory jumps in optimization
Initialization from proven 0.8279 score candidate focuses search on promising region
20 layers provide sufficient pairs for UV stopband while leaving margin under 30-layer limit
Alternating structure is manufacturable with standard thin-film deposition processes
known_risks: Uncertain whether HfO2 extinction coefficient remains negligible at 200 nm UV edge - would need measured n/k data verification
Recalled quarter-wave thickness estimates may not be exact for this specific material dataset - actual optimal thicknesses emerge from optimization
Uncertain if 20 layers is optimal vs 22, 24, or 26 for this specific band separation - layer count is fixed for this axis
Fused silica substrate dispersion in UV not precisely recalled - relies on registry dataset
No literature verification of HfO2/SiO2 UV durability under prolonged exposure - design assumes optical performance only
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Materials: alternating hfo2 and SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) layers, starting with hfo2 adjacent to air. Total 20 layers (10 hfo2, 10 SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos)). Initialize thicknesses from prior best candidate: [29.5, 39.5, 29.5, 39.5, 30.6, 39.5, 30.5, 39.5, 29.5, 39.5, 49.5, 40.5, 50.5, 40.5, 49.5, 40.5, 50.5, 40.5, 49.5, 40.0] nm. Optimize individual layer thicknesses with perturbation bounds ±0.5 nm. Wavelength bands: maximize reflectance in 200-400 nm, maximize transmittance in 800-1500 nm. Normal incidence, unpolarized. Total layers fixed at 20, materials fixed as hfo2 and SiO2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) in alternating sequence.
routes.revision_reason: Continuation refinement: reduce perturbation bounds from ±0.8 nm to ±0.5 nm and initialize from iteration 12 best candidate (0.8279088548566025 target score) to suppress oscillatory jumps and focus computational budget on refining the neighborhood of the proven optimum.

plan.knowledge_source_disclosure: This route was planned from the model's own prior knowledge alone. No Semantic Scholar query was issued, no retrieved paper reached the prompt, and no method-research report was supplied -- neither for the initial plan nor for any continuation round. It is the control arm of a controlled comparison against the literature-grounded routes, and its evidence-id allowlist is empty by construction.
unresolved_decisions: Whether 20 layers is the optimal count for this specific band separation vs 18, 22, or 24 layers - this axis fixes layer count to isolate thickness tuning effects
Exact HfO2 and SiO2 n/k values at 200 nm UV edge - relies on material_catalog registry data without independent verification
Whether alternating sequence starting with HfO2 vs SiO2 affects performance - this axis fixes the sequence
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If this control route fails to produce physically valid candidates after three consecutive rounds with relaxed perturbation bounds, the thickness-only optimization axis is exhausted and a different strategy (layer count variation or sequence variation) would be needed.

expected_observations: best_target_score should rise or remain stable across rounds as perturbation bounds narrow
valid_candidates count should remain high (≥7) given small perturbation from valid seed
tightest_margin should not fall significantly across rounds if optimization converges smoothly
thicknesses_nm should show reduced variance compared to prior ±0.8 nm rounds
run_status should remain 'completed' without physical validity failures
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 5 for two consecutive rounds, relax perturbation bounds to ±0.7 nm and continue
if tightest_margin falls below 0.3 for two consecutive rounds, reduce optimization step size and continue

selection.user_question:
我负责一款用于高空无人机短波红外遥感相机的前端防护窗口研发。相机需要尽可能完整地接收 800–1500 nm 波段的短波红外目标信号，同时尽可能反射 200–400 nm 波段的紫外辐射，以减少太阳紫外杂散光进入探测器，并降低长期紫外辐照对探测器和后端光学组件的影响。

请在空气入射、熔融石英基底的条件下设计一个平面多层介质膜。膜层材料仅允许使用 HfO2 和 SiO2，膜系总层数不超过 30 层。在这些材料和层数限制下，希望同时获得 800–1500 nm 波段的高透射率和 200–400 nm 波段的高反射率。

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.
